completed_iter27: TASK-018A versioned HTTP API contract + semantic compatibility gate + SDK parity, implemented and verified on task/TASK-018A-api-contract-sdk-compatibility (not yet merged). agentrouter/contract.py exports a canonical byte-stable OpenAPI document to contracts/http/v1/openapi.json with provenance in a sibling manifest.json (deliberately not in the contract, so an unchanged API produces an unchanged file). `agentrouter contract export|check [--json] [--out]` exits 0 compatible / 1 breaking / 3 missing-or-untrustworthy baseline; a missing baseline is never a pass; export refuses to overwrite a breaking change and accepting one requires --accept-breaking --reason, appended to a history a later export cannot erase. New CI job api-compatibility; enforce-release-gate now needs it; ci.yml and security.yml pinned to permissions: contents: read.

THE GATE WAS GUARDING NOTHING, TWICE — both fixed. (1) Four of nine operations were declared `-> dict`, so the exported contract said only 'an object' for their responses and a renamed or removed field on /v1/classify, /v1/route, /v1/decisions/{id} or /v1/execute/dry-run produced no diff at all. Now typed response envelopes with extra='allow', verified against live payloads so nothing is stripped from the wire (route 14 keys, decision 16, dry-run 7, classify 12 all preserved). (2) Auth was a bare X-API-Key Header parameter, indistinguishable in the export from any other optional header, so adding or removing authentication on an endpoint was invisible. Now a declared APIKeyHeader security scheme.

SECURITY REVIEW — 2 HIGH on the pre-existing server, both real, both fixed with regression tests. (1) @app.exception_handler(Exception) was registered on Starlette's OUTERMOST middleware, above request_id_middleware, so it never ran: an unhandled fault was answered by ServerErrorMiddleware with no envelope and no X-Request-ID. Now converted inside request_id_middleware AND logged at ERROR with a redacted traceback, because catching it there also stops the ASGI server logging it - otherwise a leaky 500 would have become a silent one. (2) The RegistryError handler returned str(exc), which interpolates the registry path and the offending YAML source line; a registry is malformed at exactly the moment someone has pasted a credential into it, so this returned that credential to an UNAUTHENTICATED caller on /v1/models and /ready. Both now answer registry_unavailable with a fixed message, detail to the log only. /ready no longer catches RegistryError itself, so readiness and the /v1 routes report the same code for the same condition.

A GATE YOU CAN EDIT IS NOT A GATE. An unresolvable, self-referential or remote $ref inlined as {} and made a schema look permissive, so a one-character edit to the committed baseline turned CI green - load_baseline now refuses such a document. $ref expansion is bounded by node and depth budgets (a fan-out document would otherwise OOM). Export refuses to follow a symlink or write outside the repo root. The acceptance history records only the changes the checker itself found, so it cannot assert a breaking change that never happened, and a later routine export cannot erase it.

MY OWN TEST FOUND THE NEXT BUG: validate_refs re-walked every path, so a 26-level fan-out document took 2**26 steps - 66 seconds on a contract small enough to read by eye. The check meant to protect CI would have hung it. Memoising validated refs (the DFS stack still detects cycles) took the contract suite from 66s to 3.5s. Also fixed a classification bug: introducing maxLength where there was none was reported as merely risky because an absent bound was treated as unknown. An absent bound is the unbounded END of the range, so introducing one rejects every longer request that used to be valid - it is now correctly BREAKING.

SDK PARITY IS EVIDENCE, NOT A CLAIM. contracts/sdk/capabilities.json lists nine operations and every one is exercised against the real app: Python via in-process uvicorn on loopback, TypeScript via scripts/serve_for_parity.py. The TS suite previously only asserted the requests it BUILT, which cannot catch a well-formed request the server rejects. CI sets AGENTROUTER_REQUIRE_LIVE=1 so a skipped live suite fails rather than passing quietly (verified: skips cleanly without it, exits 1 with it).
